title: Breaking: The Sun Went Out
description: A total eclipse rolls over town at noon, and Snazzie FM covers it like a missing-persons case for the sun. Ronnie refuses to accept it was scheduled and starts negotiating with the sky on air, while new astronomer Doctor Vasquez insists totality ends at two minutes seventeen, right up until her stopwatch keeps not ending.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: We are cutting away from the noon hour on Snazzie FM, because folks, the sun has gone out. I want to be calm about this. The sun. Our sun. Is not currently on.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Ronnie, it's an eclipse. It was in the paper. There were glasses at the gas station.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: The paper does not schedule the sun, Barry. <p:0.3> We've brought in a professional. Our brand new station astronomer, Doctor Vasquez. Doctor, you're on the air.

lines.speaker: vasquez
lines.text: Thank you, Ronnie. And everyone please relax, because this is a textbook total solar eclipse. I have it on the watch. Totality ends at two minutes seventeen. To the second.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Two minutes seventeen. <p:0.3> And until then, the sky is just allowed to take our sun?

lines.speaker: vasquez
lines.text: It's not taking it, it's in front of it. The moon is in front of it.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: So we DO have a suspect. <p:0.3> Stay with me, big guy. We're gonna get you home. Nobody up there move.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Who are you talking to, Ronnie. The sun cannot hear the radio.

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: Ronnie, if I may. As I have said for YEARS, the sun would go dark at precisely this hour, and did a single one of you write it down? No. You did not credit me.

lines.speaker: vasquez
lines.text: You did not predict this, sir, an entire field of astronomy predicted this. <p:0.3> And we are coming up on it now. Watch. Three, two, one. <p:0.4> Okay. The number is two minutes forty. It revises. It's fine.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: It revised, Barry. <p:0.3> The doctor's own number revised. The sun has blown past its release date.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: It's a rounding thing. The math is fine, Ronnie.

lines.speaker: caller-sal
lines.text: Hey, while we wait, who needs eclipse glasses? I got the last pair in the county. <p:0.3> Twenty bucks. Cash. I will meet you in a dark parking lot, which is all of them right now.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Sal, we are negotiating with the sky and you are running a yard sale.

lines.speaker: caller-gary
lines.text: Ooooooh. <p:0.4> Oooooooooh. <p:0.3> Dark.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Gary, do you have anything other than that.

lines.speaker: caller-gary
lines.text: Oooooooh.

lines.speaker: vasquez
lines.text: Okay, the watch now reads three ten, which is, that's a long totality, that's an unusually generous totality, but the model accommodates it. The model is comfortable. <p:0.3> I am comfortable.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Doctor, you said two seventeen like it was a vow. <p:0.3> Now look at us.

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: Three ten. As I have said for YEARS, it would overshoot, and once again, no acknowledgment, no plaque, nothing.

lines.speaker: caller-sal
lines.text: Glasses are thirty now, the dark's been going a while, supply and demand!

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: I am going up the chain. <p:0.3> Sky. Whoever's running the sky. This is the anchor. I want my sun back and I want it back warm.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Ronnie, it's an eclipse, it ends on its own, you do not have to TALK to it.

lines.speaker: vasquez
lines.text: It should have ended. <p:0.4> It really should have ended, Barry. I have stopped the watch. I've stopped it. There's no point timing something that won't end.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: She stopped the WATCH. <p:0.3> Folks, the scientist has stopped counting. That's a Level Four. Bring in the candles.

lines.speaker: caller-gary
lines.text: Dark.

lines.speaker: vasquez
lines.text: The watch is fine. <p:0.3> I need everyone to hear me. The watch is completely fine. The sun is the problem.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Come back to us, buddy. Nobody's mad. <p:0.3> You come back over that ridge and we forget the whole thing.

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: I called it!

lines.speaker: caller-sal
lines.text: Glasses are FIFTY!

lines.speaker: vasquez
lines.text: The watch is FINE!

lines.speaker: caller-gary
lines.text: Dark!

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Stay with me, big guy!

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: There it is. <p:0.4> See? It came back. Told you. It always comes back.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Then where did it GO, Barry. <p:0.4> For three minutes. <p:0.3> Where does a sun GO.

lines.speaker: vasquez
lines.text: My watch says it was thirty seconds.

lines.speaker: caller-sal
lines.text: Sun's back, so glasses are five bucks now. Demand cratered. Anyone? <p:0.3> Anyone.
